overview: Letters (1935): Japanese consul Sawada introduces Mrs. Hosken to State's Dooman regarding a proposed pharmaceutical trade venture with Hoshi Pharmaceutical; Dooman agrees to assist.

people.name: Eugene H. Dooman
people.role: Official in the U.S. Department of State's Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Renzo Sawada
people.role: Consul General of Japan in New York

people.name: William M. Hosken
people.role: Representative of the Hosken Trading Company of New York

people.name: Hajime Hoshi
people.role: Representative of the Hoshi Pharmaceutical Company

people.name: A. Hadskin
people.role: Secretary of Hosken Trading Company; identification uncertain because the name is from an OCR rendering of a signature

subfiles.title: Hosken Trading Company letter arranging Mrs. Hosken's interview
subfiles.from: Hosken Trading Co., Inc., signed by its secretary (OCR: “a hadskin”)
subfiles.to: Eugene Dooman, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: The company advises Dooman of Mrs. Hosken's arrival in Washington and asks him to choose a convenient time to meet her.
subfiles.summary: Hosken Trading reports Sawada arranged Dooman's willingness to see Mrs. Hosken, giving her Washington hotel and schedule.

subfiles.title: Sawada introduction of Mrs. Hosken and pharmaceutical trade proposal
subfiles.from: Renzo Sawada, Consulate General of Japan, New York
subfiles.to: Eugene Dooman, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Sawada introduces Mrs. Hosken and describes her proposed pharmaceutical trade cooperation with Hajime Hoshi.
subfiles.summary: Sawada introduces Mrs. Hosken's pharmaceutical trade proposal with Hoshi, asking Dooman to interview her.

subfiles.title: Dooman reply promising assistance to Mrs. Hosken
subfiles.to: Renzo Sawada, Consul General of Japan
subfiles.about: Dooman acknowledges Sawada's introduction and agrees to assist Mrs. Hosken if she calls on him.
subfiles.summary: Dooman acknowledges Sawada's introduction, promising Mrs. Hosken appropriate assistance if she visits.

interest: Shows a Japanese consul's introduction connecting an American merchant to a State pharmaceutical specialist.
